'''Visas for Working Across Borders''' is the hub for the immigration side of the [[Making Money Certificate Pathways|certificate pathways]] shelf. A credential tells an employer you can do the work. A visa decides whether you are allowed to be paid for it, and where.

The two questions run in opposite directions and both are covered here:
* '''An American going out.''' Teaching, performing, research, ministry and skilled work abroad — mostly reached through an employer's sponsorship in the destination country, and in several fields through programmes that exist specifically to place foreigners.
* '''Someone coming in.''' The United States classifications that let a congregation, an institute, a school or a company bring a person here lawfully and pay them.

''Everything in this shelf is general information about published classifications and programmes, not legal advice. Immigration rules change frequently — the R-1 rule change of January 2026 is a recent example — so verify against the issuing authority before acting.''

== United States classifications ==

* '''[[The R-1 Religious Worker Visa]]''' — ministers and religious workers; the organisation petitions, not the worker. Includes ''Church of the Holy Trinity v. United States'' (1892), the decision the whole religious-worker exception descends from.
* '''[[The O-1 Visa Extraordinary Ability]]''' — extraordinary ability in the sciences, education, business, athletics or the arts. No annual cap. The eight criteria, the final merits determination, and the consultation requirement.
* '''[[Teaching and Exchange Visas J-1 and Coming to Teach in America]]''' — the exchange-visitor programme, which is the main lawful route for a foreign teacher, scholar, camp counsellor or au pair to work in the United States.

Three further categories are worth knowing by name even though they have no article here yet:
* '''P''' — athletes, artists and entertainers, including the P-3 category for '''culturally unique''' performance, which is the one that fits traditional and religious performing arts.
* '''EB-1A''' and '''EB-2 National Interest Waiver''' — the permanent categories that may be '''self-petitioned''', with no employer and no job offer. The evidence an O-1 record produces is substantially the evidence these want.
* '''TN''' — professionals from Canada and Mexico under the USMCA, a list that includes ''Teacher''.

== Going abroad ==

* '''[[Getting Paid to Teach Abroad]]''' — how sponsorship actually works, what the recurring requirements are, and the government programmes that recruit foreigners directly.

== The connecting idea ==

Both directions run on the same fuel: '''a documented record'''. A visa officer, like an employer, is reading a file. Certificates, examinations, publications, references, a verifiable employer and a clean record are what that file is made of, and they are what the [[Making Money Certificate Pathways|credential shelf]] exists to help assemble.

That is why these two subjects sit together. For a great many people the obstacle to being paid abroad is not ability and not willingness — it is that nobody told them which classification their life already fits.

Credential programmes across fourteen industries are indexed at [https://credentials.soapbox.community credentials.soapbox.community].
